meta.purpose: The audit trail behind the shop: what was observed, what could not be confirmed, and where a reviewer can check it. The reader-facing pages never state a value that is not traceable to something on this page.
meta.method: Server-side page fetch with redirects followed. The final URL, document title and breadcrumb were read from the returned page. Two of the five links had been recorded by an earlier session as returning the Amazon homepage or a bot checkpoint; both returned product pages in this pass, and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved in the site's favour.
limitations: The fetch client is bot-like; Amazon served a mobile 'product summary' variant with plpRedirect=mhFallback for every resolved link. A signed-in browser may see a different page or an interstitial.
One observation is a point-in-time event. It does not establish a stable destination.
No price, rating, review count or availability was recorded. Values seen on the page belonged to carousel cards and could not be attributed to the observed listing with confidence.
No tracking parameter visible in any observed URL matches shopnow047c-20. Whether the redirector attaches it server-side on a real click is unverified.

sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”
sources.used_for: The disclosure wording in the strip and the footer.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — section 2(a) and 2(b), Special Links
sources.quote: Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you. … you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.
sources.used_for: Why every buy link is a direct amazon.com/dp/ URL carrying ?tag=shopnow047c-20.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — section 2(b), prices and availability
sources.quote: your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License.
sources.used_for: The reason no price, rating or stock figure appears anywhere on this site.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies — section 2(b), misleading claims and limited-time promotions
sources.quote: You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices. … You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.
sources.used_for: Why the shop carries no deal badges, countdowns or performance claims of its own.

sources.title: Associates Program Commission Income Statement — section 2, disqualified purchases
sources.quote: any Product purchased by a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site by a link that is generated or displayed on a search engine … (d) … by a link that sends users indirectly to an Amazon Site via an intermediate site, without requiring the customer to click on a link or take some other affirmative action on that intermediate site (a “Redirecting Link”)
sources.used_for: Why no paid search is planned on Amazon marks, and why the buy buttons point straight at Amazon rather than through a redirector.

sources.title: Understanding ASINs (Amazon Seller Central blog)
sources.quote: “ASIN” stands for “Amazon Standard Identification Number.” It’s a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store. … The ASIN appears after “/dp/”.
sources.used_for: Distinguishing the 9-character submitted short-link codes from the 10-character ASINs observed on the destination pages.

sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
sources.quote: if there’s a connection between an endorser and the marketer that a significant minority of consumers wouldn’t expect and it would affect how they evaluate the endorsement, that connection should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
sources.used_for: The placement rule: the disclosure sits above the first buy link on every page rather than in the footer alone.

sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking — affiliate and network marketing
sources.quote: You should disclose the affiliate relationship both in the videos and in the description near the links.
sources.used_for: The rule that a disclosure near the link itself is required in addition to a site-wide statement.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.
sources.used_for: rel="sponsored" on every outbound Amazon link.

sources.title: Intro to Product structured data
sources.quote: When you add structured data to your product pages, your product information can appear in richer ways in Google Search results.
sources.used_for: The decision to mark up product and breadcrumb data — and the decision not to publish Review or Offer markup, because there are no reviews or offers to state.

flags.title: The submitted codes are not ASINs
flags.detail: All five submitted codes are nine characters. Amazon defines an ASIN as a unique ten-character alphanumeric code. The codes are short-link slugs, not product identifiers. The shop records the submitted slug and the observed ASIN in separate fields, and never substitutes one for the other.
flags.review_action: If you intended these slugs to be ASINs, they are not. Nothing needs changing on the site unless the intended products differ from the five observed.

flags.title: Tracking attribution to shopnow047c-20 is unconfirmed
flags.detail: No observed destination URL visibly carried the tag parameter. Amazon requires the Associates ID as a URL parameter on each link. Whether the short-link redirector attaches the tag server-side on a real click cannot be seen from a fetch.
flags.review_action: One click, signed in, and check the tracking report. Record the date and the result.

flags.title: Compliance status of the link.amazon short links remains unresolved
flags.detail: The links redirect through a shortener. Amazon's policies prohibit a shortened link that obscures the Amazon destination, and require the tag to be a parameter on the link. The shop does not claim the supplied links are invalid, and does not use them for its buy buttons. It links directly to tagged amazon.com/dp/ URLs instead, and lists the supplied link on each product page for transparency.
flags.review_action: Run the one-link test. If the redirector preserves the tag and lands visibly on Amazon, the supplied links can be reconsidered.

flags.title: No commission rate is known or used
flags.detail: The commission schedule sits behind the Associates sign-in. No rate is published, and no revenue, earnings estimate or forecast appears anywhere on the site.
flags.review_action: Read the rate card while signed in and record it with a date if it is ever needed for a calculation.

flags.title: No price, rating, review count or availability is published anywhere
flags.detail: Program Policies 2(b) permits these only where Amazon serves the link carrying the data, or where it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. Neither condition holds, so the absence is policy-driven and permanent until the API is connected.
flags.review_action: Apply for Creators API access if live prices are wanted. See SUG-22.

flags.title: Same-day observations disagree for three of five links
flags.detail: Three links were recorded by an earlier session as returning the Amazon homepage or a bot checkpoint, and returned product pages in this pass. Amazon varies its response by client and time. A single observation does not establish a stable destination, and the site does not present one as settled.
flags.review_action: Repeat the observation over several days, or confirm destinations inside the Associates workflow instead of by fetch.

flags.title: The appliances have not been tested
flags.detail: Every capability statement on this site is the seller's own listing language, labelled as such. No measurement, no test and no hands-on comparison was performed. The FTC's guidance requires an endorsement to reflect the endorser's honest experience, which is why nothing here is framed as a verdict.
flags.review_action: Buy and test one unit at a time. See SUG-23.

flags.title: No analytics, no cookies, and therefore no traffic numbers
flags.detail: The site ships a small event script that transmits nothing unless an endpoint is configured, and none is. GitHub Pages cannot run a collector. Any statement about how many people visit or click would be invented, so none is made.
flags.review_action: Decide on a collector or a hosted analytics service. See SUG-24.

flags.title: Product imagery is illustration, not the product
flags.detail: The food photographs on this site were generated for it and show no appliance. Amazon's IP licence restricts use of Amazon-served imagery, and presenting a stock photo as the product would misrepresent it. Each image carries a caption saying what it is.
flags.review_action: Replace with genuine photographs once the appliances are tested, if desired.

flags.title: Two older sections of this repository still publish overlapping pages
flags.detail: The repository root and crisp/ contain earlier publications covering the same topics. This session did not edit them because they belong to other sessions' scopes. They are listed on the Site map page so they can be retired deliberately.
flags.review_action: Decide between redirect, archive or leave. See SUG-16.
